_what_this_is: The ruling that a printed label may be mapped to a field and a printed value read into a canonical form, plus the labels and forms that ruling covers. src/readings.py derives its label map from LABELS here; src/gate_readings.py checks the property.

RULING.rule: A printed label may be mapped to a field, and a printed value may be read into a canonical form. Both are READINGS, not corrections: the store keeps what the source printed, the reading sits beside it labelled derived, and it can be recomputed or withdrawn without touching a claim.
RULING.precedent: birth_date_as_printed, which already carries the printed string beside the parsed date.
RULING.map_only_the_unambiguous: Where a label is not clearly a field, leave it and COUNT it. guide.Aye, guide.A ge, guide.Cracral Information, guide.Prafessional Record and guide.Hionors are OCR damage; guide.GIANTS vs. PORTSMOUTH, guide.Total Yards Gained and guide.Longest Punt are section headings and club statistics, not person fields. Mapping any of them would be inventing structure the source does not have.
RULING.refusals_are_counted_never_silent: A value that cannot be read without guessing is left as printed and counted. gate_readings prints the count on every run. A silent refusal would be the same defect in a new coat.
RULING.why: The bio panel was manufacturing disagreements between sources that agree. 51 of 73 unparsable guide heights agree with PFA once read as digits (PFA 6-1 against the guide's '61"'), and 182 of 275 sampled draft disagreements are one selection under two club vocabularies (GNB/GB, SFO/SF, NWE/NE, TAM/TB). A fabricated disagreement is worse than a hole: a hole you can see, while this looks like scholarship -- two sources, both cited, honestly held apart -- and it survives every gate, because the gates check that disagreements are HELD, and they were being held faithfully, having been invented.

A_DISAGREEMENT_IS.rule: More than one distinct READING among the values of a field. Two values that read to the same thing are one value written twice, not a disagreement.
A_DISAGREEMENT_IS.unread_values_take_no_part: A value that cannot be read can neither corroborate nor contradict, so it is excluded from the test, kept on the panel verbatim, and counted.
A_DISAGREEMENT_IS.the_stated_limit: Two unreadable strings that genuinely differ will not be flagged. That is the price of not guessing, and the refusal count is how it stays visible.

_labels_left_as_printed: Everything else in build/guide-pre1950-delimited.json -- 80+ predicates. Notably Age/age/AGE are NOT mapped here: the field is unambiguous but nothing consumes it, and a mapping nothing reads is a note wearing a declaration's authority (see gate_declarations_are_read). guide.Aye and guide.A ge stay as printed under the ruling above.

height.why_refused: A fraction mark the scanner mangled, or more digits than a height has. 6/114" is not 6-11 and 6:142 is not 6-14; reading them would be a guess. 174 of 189 printed heights read, 15 refused.

weight.reads_to: pounds as a bare integer string
weight.why_refused: All 189 printed weights read; the 37 distinct forms are already bare integers. '180.' with a trailing point is NOT accepted -- no weight in the corpus carries one, and loosening a reader for a form that does not occur is how a reader starts guessing.

birth_date.why_refused: Only a spelled-out month is read. A bare numeric date is never reordered: 2001-12-10 and 2001-10-12 stay two different dates, because deciding which number is the day would be a correction, not a reading.

draft.reads_to: {year, league, kind, numbering} with EITHER {round, overall} OR {order} -- a DICT, not a string
draft.the_club_is_not_part_of_the_reading: Still true, and for the original reason: the club follows from the pick within a draft, which is what makes PFR's TAM and nflverse's TB one selection. What was wrong was believing the pick alone identified the draft.
draft.why_this_is_not_a_club_table_job: The club table resolves the archive's own vocabulary (GB, SF, NE, TB, KC) but not PFR's (GNB, SFO, NWE, TAM, KAN), and LV/LAC/LA do not resolve either. Teaching it a second source's draft vocabulary is a separate ruling; comparing selections by pick number does not need one.
draft._object_forms_also_read: PFR's and nflverse's {year, round, overall_pick, team} and PFA's draft_selection object both read by their year/round/overall_pick fields. They are not listed under accepted_forms_by_example because that list is checked as literal strings by gate_readings R1.
draft._the_overall_pick_ordinal_is_optional: Pro Football Archives prints both '(80th overall)' and '(86 overall)'. Requiring the suffix left five of its own selections unreadable. Widened 2026-09-07 under the same principle as gate_readings R3: a reader that cannot read the archive hides real disagreements while claiming to remove false ones.

_CORRECTED_2026_09_08.what_was_wrong: This entry read to `YYYY r{round} p{overall}` and justified excluding the club with: 'An overall pick number is unique within a draft year, so year+round+overall IS the selection.' THAT PREMISE IS FALSE.
_CORRECTED_2026_09_08.measured: Across the whole range, 1936-2025: 72 of 90 years hold more than one draft numbering its picks from 1, and one year holds five. 1950 has an NFL draft and an AAFC allocation draft -- overall pick 1 is Leon Hart in one and Chet Mutryn in the other. 1965 has NFL, AFL and CFL.
_CORRECTED_2026_09_08.the_fix: league and kind are IN THE READING, where a consumer has to see them, instead of inside a value where they can be ignored. They were always present as league_from_filename and draft_kind; nothing was obliged to look.
_CORRECTED_2026_09_08.silence_is_not_a_difference: league and kind are OMITTED when unknown, never filled with a placeholder. reading_view.same() compares dict readings on the fields BOTH carry, so a record stating no league still matches one that does -- which is right, because 135 contested rows are a source declining to name the league, not a second draft. A placeholder would turn that silence into a claim.
_CORRECTED_2026_09_08.what_it_cost: 5 people had two genuinely different selections -- one AFL and one NFL, or NFL and USFL -- read identically and folded into one, which is the direction that loses information silently. And 1,783 contested rows were two TRUE selections recorded as a disagreement: a man drafted by both the AAFC and the NFL was drafted twice, and that is a fact, not a conflict.

_ORDER_RULING_2026_09_08.the_rule: An expansion, allocation or dispersal selection has an ORDER and no round. The reading carries `order`; `round` and `overall` are ABSENT.
_ORDER_RULING_2026_09_08.why_absent_and_not_zero_or_null: Absent is the only one of the three that means the document does not say. A zero would sort as a round; a null is a value and would compare as one. PFA prints these pages with the columns `Team | Player | Pos | College | Notes` -- there is no Round column and no Overall column on them at all.
_ORDER_RULING_2026_09_08.why_a_numbering_FIELD_was_also_needed: Omitting round and overall is not sufficient, and the gate proved it before this was written. `same()` compares the fields BOTH readings carry, so an ordered selection and a numbered one would have shared only year and league and been called ONE selection -- the same rule that rightly protects an unstated league would have joined a 1960 AFL allocation pick to a 1960 AFL draft pick. `numbering` is stated by both forms and by neither silently, so the difference is compared instead of assumed away.
_ORDER_RULING_2026_09_08.what_it_covers: 602 pfa.draft_allocation claims and 91 pfa.draft_selection claims now read, where they read as nothing before. Roughly 1,631 further rounds-free selections sit on 26 cached PFA pages, unread.
_ORDER_RULING_2026_09_08.what_it_does_NOT_cover: 461 pfa.draft claims are printed strings naming a SITTING and no number at all -- `First Selections 1960 Dallas Texans`. They have no round, no pick and no order, so they stay unreadable. An order invented from row position would be a fact the document does not contain.
_ORDER_RULING_2026_09_08.still_needing_a_ruling: `pfa.draft_allocation` is not a member of the draft family, so nothing downstream reads these claims yet. MEASURED, not done: adding it would create 1,995 ordered-against-existing pairs across 580 people and fold NONE of them. That is Ryan's call, because family membership changes what the contested table holds.

college.reads_to: the school, lower-cased, abbreviation expanded, the word University dropped
college.ruled: Ryan, 2026-09-07: College reads by dropping the abbreviation and the word University, so Ohio St. and Ohio State are one school.
college.why_refused: a placeholder is not a school. An empty or 'none' value is left as printed and takes no part.
college.St_IS_EXPANDED_ONLY_AS_THE_LAST_WORD: Ohio St. is Ohio State; St. Mary's is Saint Mary's. Position separates them and position is all that is used -- reading St. Mary's as State Mary's would be a guess wearing a reading's clothes.
college.College_IS_NEVER_DROPPED: Boston College and Boston University are two schools. Dropping both words would make them one, and a false agreement is worse than the two disagreements it hides. Only University goes.
college._the_stated_limit: A value carrying a trailing attendance year -- 'University of Tulsa (1940-42).', the LA Dons guide's house style -- does not collapse against 'Tulsa'. The year is not part of the school's name, but removing it is a second reading and was not ruled. 26 guide values are affected; they stay recorded as disagreements until someone rules on it.

COLLEGE_SYNONYMS._ruled: Ryan, 2026-09-07: a college abbreviation folds only when it has EXACTLY ONE possible school. Where two real schools compete for the same short form it does not fold, and the pair stays a disagreement -- which is correct.
COLLEGE_SYNONYMS._built_from: the 28 reading-gap rows measured on the Ghosts of the Gridiron ingest, 2026-09-08 -- ten distinct pairs. NOT from a general list of American colleges: a list nobody measured is a list nobody can defend. EXTENDED 2026-09-08 from the 18,279 college disagreements measured between PFA's 2,926 team-season roster tables and the archive -- 662 distinct one-to-one pairs over 14,615 rows. Every fold and every refusal is in src/measure_college_synonyms.py and build-reports/college-synonyms.json, with the evidence that decided it.
COLLEGE_SYNONYMS._the_shape_it_refuses: `Miami` could be Miami of Ohio or Miami in Florida and both played football. Same shape as the state rule's refusal of a lone `LA`, and the same shape as the college reading's own refusal to drop `College` -- Boston College and Boston University are two schools.

refuses.georgetown vs georgetown dc: Georgetown University in DC and Georgetown College in Kentucky BOTH played football. The archive's own value writes `(DC)` precisely to distinguish them, which is evidence the ambiguity is real and not theoretical.
refuses.cornell vs cornell col: Cornell University in New York and Cornell College in Iowa both played football. The archive writes `Cornell Col.` to separate them.
refuses.nebraska vs nebraska wesleyan: Nebraska and Nebraska Wesleyan are two different schools, both of which played football. A prefix is not an abbreviation.
refuses.lebanon vs lebanon valley: THE CLOSEST CALL, and refused for consistency rather than certainty. `Lebanon` is a prefix of `Lebanon Valley`, which is exactly the shape of `Nebraska` against `Nebraska Wesleyan` -- and there the prefix is a different school. Folding one prefix while refusing the other would mean the rule was really 'fold where I happen to know of no competitor', which is not a rule. Stays a disagreement.

_how_a_pair_qualifies.three_named_shapes: A short form folds only when it is (1) the INITIALISM of the long form, with or without the University that the long form omits -- USC, UBC and UNLV carry it in front, LSU, SMU, TCU and BYU behind; (2) the long form with a trailing GENERIC word dropped -- `bowling green state` to `bowling green`; or (3) the long form with its LAST word shortened -- `boston college` to `boston col`. Anything else is a guess about which school is meant, and is refused on shape.
_how_a_pair_qualifies.state_is_not_always_generic: `State` is NOT dropped where what remains is a state's own name. South Carolina State and South Carolina are two real universities, as are South Dakota's; there `State` is the whole of the distinction, and dropping it merges two schools instead of expanding an abbreviation. Two pairs were folded by an earlier version of this rule and are now refused.
_how_a_pair_qualifies.a_rival_must_be_a_rival: A second school competes only when it could ITSELF abbreviate to that short form. `usc` disagrees with `davidson` twice in the corpus -- that is one man's college disputed between two sources, not evidence that USC is ambiguous. Counting every disagreement as a rival refused all ten pairs Ryan named.
_how_a_pair_qualifies.a_fused_cell_is_not_a_school: `tcu ohio state` looks like a school beginning with `tcu` and is two colleges in one cell. It is distinguished by the remainder: if what follows the short form is itself a college the archive holds, the value is a fused cell and says nothing about ambiguity. `georgetown dc` survives that test, because `dc` is not a college.

COLLEGE_SYNONYMS._the_shortened_word_rule: Ruled by Ryan, 2026-09-08, after 14 candidates surfaced on the 1,444 team-season pages fetched that day: a shortened NON-FINAL word is the same shape as a shortened last word. `eastern michigan` and `east michigan` are one school. SHORTENING a word is not DROPPING one -- which is why `minnesota state-mankato` to `minn state-mankato` folds and `minnesota state-mankato` to `minnesota state` still does not: one token shorter, not one token fewer. Comparison is token by token with hyphens split out, so `tennessee-chattanooga` and `tenn-chattanooga` line up and a hyphen is never mistaken for part of a word; the separators must match too. THE REFUSAL TEST IS UNCHANGED and did real work here: `texas a&m` vs `texas`, `northwestern state` vs `northwestern`, `mississippi college` vs `mississippi` and `san diego state` vs `san diego` all fit the shape and are all refused, because the corpus holds a second school the short form could equally be.

birth_place.reads_to: the place as printed, with a TRAILING country token removed, a TRAILING state abbreviation expanded to the state's name, and case and punctuation folded
birth_place.ruled: Ryan, 2026-09-07, conditionally: add it if the trailing USA fold is clean across all pairs. MEASURED CLEAN -- of 2,874 people holding more than one birth place, 995 collapse and every collapse is a trailing country token (589), a trailing space (383), punctuation (22) or case (1). No collapse is semantic.
accepted_forms_by_example: Los Angeles, CA  ==  Los Angeles, California, U.S
New York, NY  ==  New York, New York
Washington, DC  ==  Washington, District of Columbia
birth_place.why_refused: a bare country is not a place this can compare; it is left as printed and takes no part.
birth_place.NOTHING_ELSE_IS_REMOVED: The city and the state stay, in the order printed. Reducing a place to its city would make Springfield, IL and Springfield, MA one place; a fold that can do that is not a reading. The city-only fold was measured (2,392 of 2,872 birth places and 603 of 723 death places 'agree' under it) and is REFUSED for exactly that reason.
birth_place._the_country_token_has_four_printed_form: USA, U.S, U.S. and 'United States'. Wikipedia writes 'U.S' and PFA writes 'USA'; reading only 'USA' left 1,808 pairs looking like disagreements over a country name. A trailing token only -- 'US Virgin Islands' keeps its US, because it is not trailing.

ruled_state_expansion.ruled: Ryan, 2026-09-07: `Los Angeles, CA` and `Los Angeles, California` are one place.
ruled_state_expansion.scope: ONLY the last token, and only when something precedes it. The fifty states and DC, by USPS abbreviation.
ruled_state_expansion.why_position_is_the_whole_rule: `IN`, `OR`, `OK`, `ME`, `LA`, `DE`, `MS`, `MT`, `PA` and `HI` are English words as well as states. Position is what separates them, and position is all that is used -- the same discipline that expands `St.` to State only as a college's last word.
ruled_state_expansion.a_qualifier_is_not_a_state: `near Whitesboro, TX` reads to `near whitesboro texas` and `Whitesboro, Texas` to `whitesboro texas`. They still DISAGREE, because one source says the town and the other says somewhere nearby, and that difference was never about the state name.
ruled_state_expansion.no_city_is_ever_dropped: `Springfield, IL` and `Chicago, IL` stay two places.
ruled_state_expansion.measured_before_it_was_added: Predicted 1,873 of 2,601 place contests would collapse. The reading collapses 1,867 -- SIX FEWER, which is the safe direction. A fold larger than the prediction would have meant it was reaching past the state name.
ruled_state_expansion.the_six_it_declines: A place that is a bare state and nothing else: `FL` against `Florida, U.S`, and five like it (`IL`, `MN`, `TN`, `NJ`, `TX`). They are the same state written two ways and Ryan's own wording ('TX and Texas are the same state and collapse') would fold them -- but a LONE token cannot be told from a city, and `LA` alone is Los Angeles at least as often as Louisiana. Left as printed and reported rather than widened. UNRULED.

death_place.reads_to: the place as printed, with a TRAILING country token removed, a TRAILING state abbreviation expanded to the state's name, and case and punctuation folded
death_place.ruled: Ryan, 2026-09-07, conditionally, as birth_place. MEASURED CLEAN, and it gains almost nothing: of 723 people holding more than one death place, exactly ONE collapses ('Washington, DC' against 'Washington, DC, United States'). Recorded so nobody re-measures it expecting a haul.

ruled_state_expansion.ruled: Ryan, 2026-09-07: `Los Angeles, CA` and `Los Angeles, California` are one place.
ruled_state_expansion.scope: ONLY the last token, and only when something precedes it. The fifty states and DC, by USPS abbreviation.
ruled_state_expansion.why_position_is_the_whole_rule: `IN`, `OR`, `OK`, `ME`, `LA`, `DE`, `MS`, `MT`, `PA` and `HI` are English words as well as states. Position is what separates them, and position is all that is used -- the same discipline that expands `St.` to State only as a college's last word.
ruled_state_expansion.a_qualifier_is_not_a_state: `near Whitesboro, TX` reads to `near whitesboro texas` and `Whitesboro, Texas` to `whitesboro texas`. They still DISAGREE, because one source says the town and the other says somewhere nearby, and that difference was never about the state name.
ruled_state_expansion.no_city_is_ever_dropped: `Springfield, IL` and `Chicago, IL` stay two places.

position.reads_to: {role, spot?, alignment?} -- a dict, like the draft reading, so that a field only one side carries is SILENCE under reading_view.same() rather than a difference.
position.ruled: Ryan, 2026-09-09. Expand the abbreviation; a SIDE is part of the position; an UNSTATED side is silence. `Halfback` does not contest `Left Halfback` -- it is less specific, and calling that a conflict is the same fabrication as `61"` against `6-1`.
position.vocabulary: declarations/positions.json -- 79 codes and 77 long forms, each spelt out WHOLE. `LS` is a Long Snapper and `LB` a Linebacker; stripping a leading `L` would make both of them Left-something.
position._what_folds: HB/LH, LB/MLB, CB/LCB, S/FS, OT/LOT, OLB/LB -- one of them states a spot and the other is silent about it.
position._what_does_not: LH/RH, MLB/SLB, FS/SS, OLB/ILB -- both state the slot and they differ. And DB/CB, E/T, KR/WR -- different roles, which is a real disagreement.
position._a_group_is_a_role: `DB` reads to Defensive Back and `CB` to Cornerback and they DO contest. Folding a group into one of its members is a rule Ryan has not made; it is the largest surviving category and it is reported rather than assumed away.
position._multi_position_is_refused: `HB-QB` states a LIST. Whether a list of two contests a list of one is not ruled; the value is unreadable, takes no part in the disagreement test, and is counted.

_documentation_only.RULING: prose addressed to a reader; src/readings.py reads LABELS and gate_readings prints RULING.rule
_documentation_only.A_DISAGREEMENT_IS: prose stating the rule the code implements
_documentation_only.VALUE_READINGS: prose, EXCEPT accepted_forms_by_example and refused_by_example, which gate_readings R1 executes against src/readings.py -- a declared form that stops reading is a gate failure
_documentation_only.ONE_RULING_ONE_DEFINITION: prose, EXCEPT known_module_name_collisions, which gate_readings R5 reads

ONE_RULING_ONE_DEFINITION.rule: A ruling has one implementation. A reading in particular must exist once, because two readers that answer differently make the archive disagree with itself about what the same fact is.
ONE_RULING_ONE_DEFINITION.why: 2026-09-07: the read service and Parsing implemented this ruling in parallel, ten minutes apart, each with its own reader and its own declaration. It did not stay theoretical for an hour -- both modules were named `readings`, service/app.py puts service/ first on sys.path, and once a name is in sys.modules every later import gets that one. bio_select asked for a reading, got the service's module, and every bio 503'd on `unhashable type: dict`. The duplication did not cause a disagreement in the answers; it caused a crash, which is the lucky version.
ONE_RULING_ONE_DEFINITION.the_definition: dataset/declarations/readings.json is the ruling; dataset/src/readings.py is the implementation. Anything else that needs a reading imports that module rather than writing a second one, and says 'no reading available' if it cannot -- never falling back to a reader that might answer differently.

ONE_RULING_ONE_DEFINITION.how_the_live_one_was_resolved: The service now loads dataset/src/readings.py BY FILE PATH under the module name archive_readings (importlib spec_from_file_location), so it cannot be satisfied by anything else called `readings` whatever is on sys.path or already in sys.modules. That is a better fix than renaming this module, because it removes import order from the question instead of betting on it.
